content: 1. The effect or concentration of selegiline may be reduced due to its metabolism being influenced by hepatic enzyme CYP2B6. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of sertraline by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 3. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of sildenafil by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. Potent CYP3A4 inducers can significantly lower sildenafil plasma levels. 4. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of solifenacin by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 5. Nevirapine decreases sorafenib levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, affects the metabolism of drugs processed by hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Co-administered CYP3A4 substrates may require dosage adjustments. 7. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of sunitinib by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 8. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of suvorexant by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce suvorexant efficacy; if dose adjustment is needed, do not exceed 20 mg/day. 9. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of tacrolimus by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 10. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of tadalafil by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid combination in pulmonary hypertension patients. For erectile dysfunction patients, monitor response carefully due to potential reduced effectiveness. 11. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of tamoxifen by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 12. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of tasimelteon by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 13. Tazemetostat reduces the effect or concentration of nevirapine by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Nevirapine also reduces the effect or concentration of tazemetostat. Use caution and monitor. 14. Tecovirimat decreases the effect or concentration of nevirapine by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness when co-administered. 15. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of temsirolimus by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 16. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of teniposide by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 17. Both nevirapine and tenofovir DF increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 18. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of theophylline by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 19. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of ticagrelor by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid using ticagrelor with potent CYP3A4 inducers. 20. Nevirapine increases the effect or concentration of tinidazole by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 21. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of tipranavir by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Both tipranavir and nevirapine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 22. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of tofacitinib by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Loss or reduced response to tofacitinib may occur when co-administered with potent CYP3A4 inducers. 23. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of tolterodine by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 24. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of toremifene by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. CYP3A4 inducers increase the rate of toremifene metabolism, lowering its steady-state serum concentration. 25. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of tramadol by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzymes CYP3A4 and CYP2B6. This results in decreased AUC of tramadol and its active metabolite (O-desmethyltramadol) when co-administered with strong inducers. 26. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 27. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of triazolam by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 28. Ublituximab reduces the effects of nevirapine due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 29. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of ubrogepant by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Dose adjustment is recommended when co-administered with moderate or weak CYP3A4 inducers. 30. Both nevirapine and valoctocogene roxaparvovec increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Medications with potential hepatotoxicity should be closely monitored, and alternative therapies considered in case of drug interactions. 31. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of vardenafil by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 32. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of verapamil by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 33. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of vilazodone by affecting its metabolism via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Consider increasing the vilazodone dose up to twofold (not exceeding 80 mg/day) when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers for more than 14 days. 34. Nevirapine decreases the effect or concentration of voriconazole by altering its metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Conversely, voriconazole increases the effect or concentration of nevirapine. Use caution and monitor. 35. Nevirapine reduces the effect or concentration of vortioxetine by increasing its metabolism. Consider increasing the vortioxetine dose when co-administered with strong CYP inducers for more than 14 days, but do not exceed three times the original dose. 36. Both nevirapine and zidovudine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 37.
